Subject: Follow-up: Clarifying retention, backups & deletion SLAs

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciated the practical questions from your team. Per our conversation I wanted to confirm a few items on retention and deletion so your compliance folks have clear notes while we prep the questionnaire answers. High-level asks from your side were: SOC 2 evidence, GDPR/HIPAA considerations for EU/PHI data, and how deletion requests interact with backups/snapshots.

A couple quick clarifying questions so we can be precise in our responses:
- Do you need the deletion SLA to guarantee removal from backups within a certain window (e.g., 30 days) or is a documented purge-on-rotation acceptable?
- Will HealthSphere require backups to be retained in a specific region for residency reasons?
- Any mandatory retention periods (e.g., 7 years for PHI) we should be aware of when proposing policy options?

I'm attaching the questionnaire you sent in the meeting notes so we can start filling it out on our side. Monica from our security team and Marissa on legal will loop in to answer the technical and contractual bits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica and Marissa to provide a written summary of default retention & backup behavior and options for shorter/longer retention.
2) We'll include a redacted SOC 2 doc for your review.
3) Book a 60-min security deep dive (SRE + Legal + Procurement).

Thanks — I’ll get Monica to take point on the questionnaire, and Marissa will add the contractual language options.

Cheers,

Ben,

Thanks for the clear recap. For context: HealthSphere will be subject to HIPAA for US PHI and GDPR for EU data. We have an internal requirement to demonstrate both:
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest available)
- Written deletion SLA for PHI that we can include in the contract (we typically ask for an ability to remove data from active storage within 24 hours and from backups within 30 days — if that’s not technically feasible we need the exact process/guarantee so our legal can evaluate).
- Log retention: security/forensic logs must be available for at least 365 days.

We also attached our vendor security questionnaire — please have the relevant teams complete it. A couple of specific questions from our info-sec reviewer:
- Do you encrypt backups at rest using customer-managed keys (CMK)?
- What is the default backup snapshot retention window and can it be shortened for specific customers?

We can do the security deep dive next week; available times Wed-Fri afternoons ET.

Appreciate the quick responses.

Best,

Hi Elaine — thanks for the specificity, that helps. Below is a concise summary of our default behavior and the contractual options we can offer. I’ve kept language consumer-friendly but can convert to legal wording for the contract.

1) SOC 2 Type II
- Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (controls redacted for customer distribution). This covers availability, security, and confidentiality control families for our hosted inference platform.

2) Default retention & logs (hosted/API)
- Request & object data (primary): default retention is customer-configurable; standard tenant data retention is 90 days unless a different retention policy is set at account creation. Deletion requests are propagated to active storage within 24 hours and will render data unrecoverable from primary stores upon completion.
- Security/forensic logs: default retention is 365 days for security-critical logs (access, audit, trace). Longer retention is available as a paid add-on.

3) Backups & snapshot behavior
- Regular managed snapshots: default snapshot retention window is 90 days. Snapshots are encrypted at rest by default using platform-managed keys.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted accounts, CMK support is available for Enterprise customers by request and subject to key-rotation/configuration review.
- Deletion from backups: our baseline operating model is snapshot rotation — when a deletion request is issued we mark the object for deletion immediately in the primary store; snapshots containing the object are scheduled for purge at the next snapshot retention cleanup. Typical purge window is up to 30 days but can be shortened for Dedicated/Private deployments or with contractual commit (we can guarantee a max 30-day backup purge window for Hosted Enterprise customers).

4) HIPAA/GDPR considerations
- PHI handling: we treat PHI under our protected-data handling program. For customers requiring stricter control (e.g., 7-year retention or particular deletion guarantees) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where we can set retention policies and purge cycles to meet regulatory needs.
- EU residency: we support region-specific storage. If HealthSphere requires EU-only storage for EU subjects, we can provision region-restricted buckets and replicating rules.

5) Contractual options we can offer
- Deletion SLA: Confirmed: active storage logical deletion within 24 hours. Backup purge: default up to 30 days; can be contractually reduced to 7–30 days for Dedicated/Private with pricing uplift.
- CMK: available for Dedicated/Private; hosted CMK for Enterprise under negotiation.
- Audit evidence: provide redacted SOC 2 report and periodic penetration-test high-level summary.

Next steps:
- I’ll populate the vendor questionnaire sections for technical controls and backups (expect a first pass within 48 hours).
- Ben: please propose two windows for the security deep dive (we have availability Thursday 27 May 2pm ET or Friday 28 May 11am ET).
- Marissa: I’ll coordinate with you on the exact SLA language for backup purge windows and any indemnity/contractual asks.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Monica / Marissa — thank you, this is helpful and much clearer. A few follow-ups before the deep dive:

- The proposed deletion SLA language (active deletion within 24 hours; backup purge within 30 days, contractually reducible to 7 days for Dedicated/Private) is acceptable as a starting point. Please prepare a sample clause we can share with our legal team that states: "On receipt of a verified deletion request from the Customer, Redwood will perform logical deletion from active storage within 24 hours and will schedule removal from managed backups within a maximum of 30 days. For Dedicated or Private deployments, Redwood will offer a contractual backup purge window of no more than 7 days upon request and subject to pricing/operational terms."

- For CMK: HealthSphere prefers customer-managed keys for backups. Please include the configuration steps and limitations for enabling CMK in Enterprise hosted accounts.

- We’d like the redacted SOC 2 (received) and the completed vendor questionnaire by COB Friday so our reviewers can prepare for the deep dive.

We can confirm the Thursday 27 May 2pm ET security deep dive — I’ll send a calendar invite to all. Procurement will be on the call as well to discuss contract language.

Thanks again — this moves things forward.

Best,
Elaine Nguyen
Director, Information Security | HealthSphere Inc.
